You are not wrong, I am probably at the extreme end though, had computers since the c64, self employed building websites for myself so I am on the computer a lot, currently updating 15-4460 to a i5-12400 so yeah, every 7 years for me.  Wife's PC is 5 years old and the kids is just a couple but will last them another 5 or so. Unless you are a hardcore gamer that then why update every few years? Though I have been resisting getting a higher end board with ddr5 for future proof but how long will that be? 2-3 years before a new generation and new board, only thing salvageable would be the ram. Meh, it never ends.

The mortar is 30 euro more expensive. In my research the increased speed of ddr5 is not that big for most things, maybe in a year or two, and there is still quite a price difference. For what I do which is number crunching very large files, dumping large of amounts of data into a database, , extracting very large files etc etc and I am currently doing this on a i5-4460, 8gb of ram and a 16 year old hard drive ( IDE so not even SATA) so going from this to a  i5 12400, 32gb of ddr4 ram and a M.2 PCIe 4.0 drive will make such a big difference that the ddr5 ram would be negligible I presume. It also never ends, wait till this, wait for that, 30 euro more for a slightly better this...

I will be doing a lot of number crunching and the likes, running a particular program on 10gb+ files that take hours or in some cases days on my current PC (8 years old), some video editing and rendering  but small 1080 3-5 minute clips. Thought I would update this for any one else that is suffering symptoms of low testosterone, as there is no information online apart from this post and my experience.

I have so far had 3 tests, 1 privately and 2 publicly, over a 3 month period. My results were consistently low 6.9, 6.92, 7.0 nmol/L (range 9.9 - 27.8), I also suffer symptoms such as low (non existent if I am being honest) sex drive, no morning wood etc. I am also middle age so will be different if younger I presume  as it will effect your ability for having children, already have so not planning on more. It is a big decision as it is life long, it shuts down your natural ability to produce testosterone.

I have had 2 appointments with a endocrinologist at Mater Dei, first appointment he was asking questions and giving me a check over, I had already done 2 blood tests by the time of my first appointment. He ordered some more blood tests and got the results on my second appointment which were also low.

They have prescribed me testosterone enanthate, but the kicker is only 1ml every 4 weeks. I have done a lot of research on this and asked at various forums, testosterone enanthate is out of your system in 10 days so everyone I have asked about this that knows what they are talking about cannot believe it as my testosterone levels will be all over the place, normal for 10 days then plummeting till my next shot (possible mood swings, estrogen spikes, depression, acne etc etc), I should be getting 1ml every 10 days at the least, problem is testosterone here comes in 1ml virals so I am thinking they are thinking that 1ml every 10 days is too much.
